rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Current Debt R&D Retrenchment" (identical multiplier, identical cash leg, only DELTA(xrd/sale) swapped for NEG(TS_RANK(xrd/sale,5))), so it re-tests the same channel rather than a substantively different mechanism.

It reuses the exact issuance multiplier and oancf/at leg of the archived "Cash Backed Equity Issuer Quality" and merely substitutes the well-worn dlc/lt maturity leg for the accrual leg, making it an incremental recombination of two already-tested components rather than a new hypothesis.

Internally consistent and a genuine reframing of the failed lagged-capital-raise idea into a profit-productivity-vs-asset-growth payoff test, though the spread leg is close to the well-known asset-growth and profitability-change anomalies and the non-negative issuance multiplier means magnitude of issuance will dominate the cross-sectional dispersion.

The construction is coherent with its stated economics (signed net retirement scaled by a [0,1] gate that is high only when both cash generation and interest burden are high) and it directly diagnoses why the earlier net-debt-retirement signal had a strong slope but no alpha; the main risk is that the high-xint/lt gate loads on distress and the gate compresses rather than reorders the signed paydown.

This is the archived "Profitable Cash Maturity Spread" with oancf/at replaced by NEG(DELTA(cogs/sale)) — same industry-profitability multiplier, same dlc/lt leg — so it is a cosmetic variant that also inherits the sign-flip of an already-tested gross-margin-squeeze idea.

Structurally this is the archived "Productive Debt Issuer Margin" with both legs differenced (margin change → cash-carry change, xint/lt level → xint/lt change), which is a delta-ization rather than a new mechanism, and it further overlaps "Levered Cash Carry Advantage" on the oancf/lt versus xint/lt comparison.
